approach: Add one required `dependents` list to the planner's output (PlanOutput), carry it as a defaulted-empty list on the JobPlan record, and refuse at admission in `plan_findings` (Major finding, so the plan returns to the planner with no critic call) when the list is empty or an entry has neither a test nor an unaffected-reason. Each entry is flat: the changed item, the dependent (path or name), its kind (code, rule, host_setting), and a test or a reason. planner.md gains the requirement and critic.md gains its own "what else does this break" question, which checks the list against a repository search. plan_body renders the list only when it is non-empty, so old records keep the same producer-section bytes and SHA-256. The CI-reuse replay is a test in admission.rs. It builds the CI-reuse plan inputs (the change makes `runs_from_record` in checks.rs return a CheckRun with `exit_code: None, reused: true`). It runs a real search of the crates' sources for readers of `.reused` and requires the search to find verify.rs (the seen-commands rule in `judge`). It then runs the real `plan_findings` on a section that omits verify.rs and on one that names it. Admission checks shape only; the search is the critic's job (brief) and the test's.

decisions.choice: One flat list of entries `{changed, dependent, kind, test, unaffected_reason}` instead of a changed item holding a nested dependents list.
decisions.reason: Each dependent needs its own test-or-reason, so a flat entry is the unit admission checks. The schema gets one new object (the existing test counts 6 plan objects, which becomes 7) where nesting would add two. The planner repeats `changed` across entries.

rejected.option: Nested: changed item with a list of dependents, each with test/reason
rejected.why: Two more schema object levels, a bigger record, the same information.
Admission could not tell which dependent lacks a test or reason; the rule would be prose only.

decisions.choice: The check lives in `plan_findings` as Major findings: one for an empty list (names the missing section), one per entry with a blank test and blank reason (location `dependents, <dependent>`, summary names the dependent). Also blank `changed` or `dependent` text.
decisions.reason: `plan_findings` is the model-free check; a Major finding already sends the plan back with no critic call (planning.rs line ~225). The rule is enforced by mechanism, not only by prose.

rejected.why: Parse failure stops the job with 'no valid plan' instead of letting the planner revise.
Minor findings do not stop a plan.

decisions.choice: `PlanOutput.dependents` is required (no serde default, and the hardened schema lists it as required). `JobPlan.dependents` is `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty")]`, and `JobPlan::validate` does not demand it.
decisions.reason: New planner output must carry it. Stored records without the field must parse and re-serialize byte for byte, as the existing seam round-trip test does. Admission judges only new plans, so old records are not re-refused.

rejected.why: Two empty states; Vec with skip_serializing_if gives the same compatibility with less code.
The request says no new record file and no migration.

decisions.choice: `plan_body` prints a `Dependents:` block only when the list is non-empty.
decisions.reason: `render_plan_section` is hashed into `producer_section_sha256` so the producer prompt can be rebuilt. An unconditional block would change the bytes for every stored plan. Producer, critic and revision briefs all use plan_body, so each sees the list.

rejected.why: Changes the hash input of every existing plan.

decisions.choice: The CI-reuse replay does its own repository search in the test (it walks `crates/*/src`, collects files with a non-comment line containing `.reused`, and asserts verify.rs is among them). It then runs the real `plan_findings` on two fixture sections. Only the 'named or not' comparison is test code.
decisions.reason: The brief says admission checks shape only and the critic checks truth against a search. The test therefore pairs a real search (so the fixture cannot drift from the code) with real admission. No logic sits in a double, and no model runs.

rejected.why: plan_findings is pure and has no repository access; automatic dependency analysis is out of scope.

rejected.option: Add a production `unnamed_readers` function used only by the test
rejected.why: Dead code in production. Open question 1 asks whether the owner wants it.

demonstrations.method: Test `ci_reuse_replay_requires_dependents_to_name_the_seen_commands_rule` in the admission.rs tests. Plan inputs: a JobPlan that modifies crates/athena-core/src/checks.rs (`runs_from_record`), with changed item 'CheckRun built from a CI result: exit_code None, reused true'. Step 1: search the crates' sources under CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR/../ for non-comment lines containing `.reused` and assert the hits include crates/athena-core/src/verify.rs (the seen-commands rule in `judge`). Step 2: a section naming only checks.rs and status readers leaves verify.rs unnamed, so the requirement is unmet. Step 3: a section naming verify.rs `judge` seen-commands with a test (`a_command_neither_run_nor_recorded_is_unseen_and_a_recorded_one_needs_the_same_text`) meets it and `plan_findings` adds no dependents finding. Step 4: the same entry with no test and no reason gets a Major finding naming verify.rs.
demonstrations.observes: The search finds verify.rs. The section without verify.rs is reported unmet, and the section with it is met and admitted. The incomplete verify.rs entry is refused.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the section does not name verify.rs, step 2's assertion that the requirement is unmet fails. If the rule moved out of verify.rs, step 1 fails. If plan_findings ignored dependents, step 4 fails.
demonstrations.seam: Production `plan_findings` in admission.rs (exists), driven with a JobPlan literal fixture (the file-search helper and the comparison are the test's own; the step 5 edits add the fixture). The search reads the real sources, so verify.rs `judge` is the genuine rule. No model, no double.

open_questions: Admission only checks shape, so it cannot know that verify.rs ought to be named. Only the critic, by brief, and the replay test, by a real search, enforce completeness. Does the owner want a production `unnamed_readers(plan, search_hits)` function for a later mechanical search? This plan adds none.

The listed deliverables omit docs/system-facts.md, docs/records.md and the CLI tests job_plan.rs, lifecycle.rs and introspection.rs. The first is required by the budgets test. The CLI tests fail without the field. Admission will give a Minor 'outside the deliverables' finding for them. Should the reading list them?

An empty dependents list is treated as a missing section. A change that truly has no dependents must still list an entry with an unaffected_reason (for example a new file nothing reads). This is by design, but unconfirmed.

The input forms of the new refusal are the missing list, an entry with a blank test and a blank reason, a whitespace-only test or reason, blank `changed` or `dependent` text, and an entry with both. refusal_corpus.rs (`Case`, `corpus_cases_get_the_expected_outcome`, `corpus_covers_the_listed_input_forms`) exercises reading checks only. I found no case about plans, so the forms are mapped to the admission unit tests above and no corpus case is added. Please confirm that this is acceptable.
The 15% newly-refused figure in the request is an estimate. The code did not settle it: plan admission is not part of the reading replay in `athena.replay/1`.
